module.title: Unit 6: Job Descriptions & Delegating Team Responsibilities
module.objective: Mampu mendeskripsikan rincian pekerjaan dan mendelegasikan tugas menggunakan causative verbs (have/make/get).

subModules.title: Reading Mission: Sharing Work at the Office
subModules.grammarFocus: Causative verbs: have, make, and get
subModules.vocabularyFocus: Job roles, responsibilities, and managing tasks

content.summary: Read about a project manager who shares work across a team. You will identify job responsibilities, find details about deadlines, and notice how have, make, and get describe asking or persuading someone to do a task.

linguisticTarget.grammar: Use have + person + base verb for arranging a task, make + person + base verb for requiring or forcing a task, and get + person + to + base verb for persuading someone.
linguisticTarget.vocabulary: Learn words for job descriptions, supervision, responsibility, and managing a team's workload.
linguisticTarget.readingStrategy: Skim the passage first to understand the situation. Then scan for names, tasks, and deadlines. Use nearby words to work out unfamiliar vocabulary.

learningObjectives: Understand the main idea of a short text about sharing work in a project team.
Locate details about team members' tasks, responsibilities, and deadlines.
Recognize how have, make, and get are used to arrange, require, or persuade someone to do a task.

contextWarmup.prompt: Your team has a report due on Friday. What is a useful first step?
options: Check the tasks and share them among the team.
Wait until Friday to decide who will write it.
Ask one person to do every task without explaining the deadline.
contextWarmup.explanation: Checking and sharing the tasks helps the team understand its responsibilities and manage the workload.

rules: Use have + person + base verb to arrange for someone to do a task: The manager had Lee check the figures.
Use make + person + base verb when someone requires or forces another person to do something: The rules made everyone wear a badge.
Use get + person + to + base verb when someone persuades another person to do something: She got Ben to review the plan.

commonTrap.explanation: After have and make, use the base verb without to. After get + person, include to before the base verb.
commonTrap.wrong: The manager got Sam prepare the schedule.
commonTrap.correct: The manager got Sam to prepare the schedule.

content.contractionsSubtitle: In everyday speech, subjects and verbs often combine in short forms:

grammarFormulas.title: Sentence Patterns with Causative Verbs
grammarFormulas.description: Compare the verb forms used to arrange, require, or persuade someone to do a task:

items.exampleSentence: A good manager delegates tasks fairly.
The job description explains the main duties.
Nina oversees the work on the new website.
Each person is accountable for their own tasks.
We need to prioritise the client report.
The team must finish the report before the deadline.
Checking the figures is one of Lee's responsibilities.

content.passageTitle: A Clear Plan for the Team
paragraphs: Nina is a project manager at a small design company. Her job description says that she oversees client projects and helps the team meet deadlines. On Monday, the team received a request for a new website. Nina checked everyone's workload before she divided the work.

She had Lee prepare a list of the client's needs because he had spoken to the client before. She asked Maya to make the first page, and she got Omar to check the writing. Omar was busy, so Nina explained why his help was important. He agreed to do the check on Wednesday.

Nina made the whole team attend a short meeting to discuss the deadline and answer questions. She did not want one person to do everything, so she prioritised the most urgent tasks and shared the rest. Each person was accountable for their part, while Nina remained responsible for overseeing the full project.

content.summary: Learn how project leaders assign tasks using causative verbs like have, get, and make. Notice how function words link and reduce in natural workplace speech.
learningObjectives: Catch the main points during a team delegation discussion.
Identify causative verbs and understand who performs each action.
Recognize weak forms and consonant linking in connected workplace speech.

keyPhrases.note: Used for standard workplace delegation where someone follows instructions as part of their job.

keyPhrases.meaning: membujuk atau mengatur seseorang untuk melakukan sesuatu
keyPhrases.note: Used when you need to persuade or arrange for someone to complete an action.

keyPhrases.meaning: mewajibkan atau memaksa seseorang melakukan sesuatu
keyPhrases.note: Expresses strong obligation or strict requirements without exceptions.
Casual phrasal expression used when deciding task priority.

connectedSpeech.note: The pronoun 'them' drops the initial 'th' sound, and 'to' reduces to a weak schwa.
The final /z/ sound links directly to the vowel in 'us'.
The consonant /t/ links smoothly to the starting vowel sound of 'away'.
The word 'to' reduces to /tə/ and joins with 'lot'.

subModules.title: Writing Mission: Delegating Tasks and Defining Job Roles

content.summary: This guide teaches you how to write clear workplace emails and role descriptions. You will practice using causative verbs (have, make, and get) to delegate duties, enforce company guidelines, and persuade team members effectively.

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Standard Delegation with 'Have'
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + have (conjugated) + person + base verb + task/details
blueprintItems.example: The project manager will have Marcus review the client proposal this morning.

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Mandatory Requirements with 'Make'
blueprintItems.formula: Subject + make (conjugated) + person + base verb + task/details
blueprintItems.example: Company regulations make all warehouse employees wear protective helmets.

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Persuasion and Convincing with 'Get'
blueprintItems.example: Elena managed to get the design team to update the presentation slides.

mechanicsRules.rule: Never insert 'to' after causative 'have' or 'make' in active sentences.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Our supervisor made David to resubmit the sales spreadsheet.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Our supervisor made David resubmit the sales spreadsheet.
mechanicsRules.why: In active causative structures, 'make' and 'have' take a bare infinitive without the word 'to'.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always use a full infinitive ('to' + verb) after causative 'get'.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I will get the technician fix the office network before lunch.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I will get the technician to fix the office network before lunch.
mechanicsRules.why: Unlike 'have' or 'make', causative 'get' requires 'to' before the base verb.

mechanicsRules.rule: Maintain accurate third-person singular verb forms in the present tense.
mechanicsRules.badExample: The operations head have his assistant organize the files every Friday.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: The operations head has his assistant organize the files every Friday.
mechanicsRules.why: Singular subjects like 'the head' or 'the manager' require 'has' or 'makes' in present simple sentences.

sampleSentences.en: I will have our senior accountant check the invoice before we send it to the client.
sampleSentences.id: Saya akan meminta akuntan senior kami memeriksa faktur sebelum kami mengirimkannya ke klien.
sampleSentences.focus: Causative 'have' with bare infinitive for professional delegation

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using causative 'have' so that it means the manager instructed Daniel to write the summary:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The manager instructed Daniel to write the project summary.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'had Daniel write'. Remember that causative 'have' takes a bare infinitive.
targetAnswers: The manager had Daniel write the project summary.
The manager had Daniel write the project summary
practicumQuestions.explanation: In past simple, 'instructed someone to write' changes to 'had someone write' without 'to'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using causative 'get' to show that Jessica persuaded the supplier to lower the price:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Jessica persuaded the supplier to lower the equipment price.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'got the supplier to lower'. Causative 'get' requires 'to'.
targetAnswers: Jessica got the supplier to lower the equipment price.
Jessica got the supplier to lower the equipment price
practicumQuestions.explanation: Causative 'get' in the past simple is 'got' and is followed by an object and a to-infinitive ('to lower').

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the grammar mistake in the causative verb structure:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The director makes each department head to deliver a status report.
practicumQuestions.hint: Remove the unnecessary word 'to' after 'makes each department head'.
targetAnswers: The director makes each department head deliver a status report.
The director makes each department head deliver a status report
practicumQuestions.explanation: Active causative 'make' must be followed by a bare infinitive ('deliver'), not a to-infinitive.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two sentences into one using the conjunction 'because':
practicumQuestions.promptText: We had the technician inspect the printer. It stopped working during the meeting.
practicumQuestions.hint: Join the two complete clauses using 'because' without changing the order.
targetAnswers: We had the technician inspect the printer because it stopped working during the meeting.
We had the technician inspect the printer because it stopped working during the meeting
practicumQuestions.explanation: The conjunction 'because' joins the main clause with the reason clause smoothly.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence using 'makes' to express an obligatory office rule:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The firm obliges every new staff member to sign a confidentiality contract.
targetAnswers: The firm makes every new staff member sign a confidentiality contract.
The firm makes every new staff member sign a confidentiality contract
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Makes' indicates requirement and takes a bare infinitive ('sign') instead of 'to sign'.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Correct the error in the causative 'get' structure:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Can you get the maintenance crew clean the conference room before noon?
practicumQuestions.hint: Causative 'get' requires the preposition 'to' before the verb 'clean'.
targetAnswers: Can you get the maintenance crew to clean the conference room before noon?
Can you get the maintenance crew to clean the conference room before noon
practicumQuestions.explanation: Unlike 'have' and 'make', causative 'get' always requires 'to' before the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Combine the two delegation tasks into one clear sentence using 'and':
practicumQuestions.promptText: I will have Thomas draft the contract. I will have Lisa review the financial terms.
targetAnswers: I will have Thomas draft the contract, and I will have Lisa review the financial terms.
I will have Thomas draft the contract and I will have Lisa review the financial terms.
I will have Thomas draft the contract and Lisa review the financial terms.
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use 'and' to connect two related delegation actions in a compound sentence.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Write a complete sentence delegating the task of checking inventory to Kevin tomorrow using 'will have':
practicumQuestions.promptText: Delegate checking the inventory to Kevin tomorrow.
practicumQuestions.hint: Start with 'I will have Kevin check...'.
targetAnswers: I will have Kevin check the inventory tomorrow.
I will have Kevin check the inventory tomorrow
We will have Kevin check the inventory tomorrow.
We will have Kevin check the inventory tomorrow
practicumQuestions.explanation: The formula is Subject + will have + person + base verb ('check') + object + time expression.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Turn this direct instruction into a polite request using 'Could you get' and the causative form:
practicumQuestions.promptText: Tell the IT staff to reset my password.
practicumQuestions.hint: Use 'Could you get the IT staff to reset my password?'
targetAnswers: Could you get the IT staff to reset my password?
Could you get the IT staff to reset my password
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Could you get someone to do something?' is a polite and natural way to request delegation.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Fix both the subject-verb agreement and causative verb errors in this sentence:
practicumQuestions.promptText: The supervisor have the intern to print fifty copies of the agenda.
practicumQuestions.hint: Change 'have' to 'has' for third-person singular, and remove 'to' before 'print'.
targetAnswers: The supervisor has the intern print fifty copies of the agenda.
The supervisor has the intern print fifty copies of the agenda
practicumQuestions.explanation: 'The supervisor' is third-person singular, so 'have' becomes 'has'. Causative 'has' requires a bare infinitive ('print').

subModules.title: Speaking Lab: Describing Roles and Sharing Work

content.summary: Practise describing job responsibilities and sharing tasks clearly. Use have, make, and get to explain what you arrange or ask other people to do. Speak in short, complete sentences and name the person responsible for each task.
content.audioGuidance: Stress the main information words, such as job, tasks, deadlines, and accountable. Use a falling voice at the end of statements and a rising voice for yes-or-no questions. Pause briefly between responsibilities so your listener can follow your instructions.

pillars.name: Vowel Clarity
pillars.target: Clear vowel sounds in job-related words
pillars.explanation: Say the vowel in job clearly, and take care to distinguish the first vowel in workload from the vowel in work. Slow down slightly if two words sound similar.

pillars.name: Word Stress
pillars.target: Clear stress in longer work vocabulary
pillars.explanation: Give the main stress to the correct syllable in words such as delegate, accountable, and prioritise. Practise each word slowly, then use it in a full sentence.

pillars.name: Causative Verb Forms
pillars.explanation: Use have plus a person plus the base verb, as in, I had Maya check the figures. Use make plus a person plus the base verb, as in, The deadline made us work quickly. Use get plus a person plus to and the verb, as in, I got Leo to update the schedule.

pillars.name: Clear Instructions
pillars.explanation: Give one instruction at a time. Pause before stating the deadline or the person accountable, and check that the other person understands.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Delegate is stressed on the first syllable. Accountable is stressed on the second syllable.
Oversee has stress on the first syllable, while prioritise has stress on the second.
Workload is stressed on the first syllable. In job description, job and the first syllable of description are prominent.
The stress changes from the second syllable in responsible to the fourth syllable in responsibility.

drills.targetText: I delegate the weekly report to Sam, and I oversee the final review.

drills.focus: Word stress in delegate and oversee
drills.hint: Stress the first syllable of delegate and the final syllable of oversee.

drills.focus: The causative pattern have someone do something
drills.hint: After had Priya, use the base verb check, not to check.

drills.targetText: I got Omar to organise the tasks and share the workload fairly.
drills.phonetic: /aɪ ɡɒt ˈəʊmɑː tə ˈɔːɡənaɪz ðə tɑːsks ən ʃeə ðə ˈwɜːkləʊd ˈfeəli/
drills.focus: The causative pattern get someone to do something
drills.hint: Link got Omar smoothly, then make sure to comes before organise.

drills.targetText: The urgent request made the team prioritise the client report.
drills.phonetic: /ði ˈɜːdʒənt rɪˈkwest meɪd ðə tiːm praɪˈɒrətaɪz ðə ˈklaɪənt rɪˈpɔːt/
drills.focus: The causative pattern make someone do something and sentence stress
drills.hint: After made the team, use prioritise without to. Stress the important task names.

turns.translation: Deskripsi pekerjaan menyatakan bahwa kamu akan membantu menyiapkan laporan klien. Bisakah kamu membuat draf pertama?

turns.speaker: Project Assistant
turns.text: Yes. I can ask Nina to check the figures, and I will finish the draft by Wednesday.
turns.translation: Ya. Saya bisa meminta Nina memeriksa angka-angkanya, dan saya akan menyelesaikan drafnya pada hari Rabu.

turns.speaker: Team Manager
turns.text: Good. I will get Leo to organise the meeting notes, and I will oversee the final version.
turns.translation: Bagus. Saya akan meminta Leo menyusun catatan rapat, dan saya akan mengawasi versi akhirnya.

turns.speaker: Project Assistant
turns.text: That sounds fair. We can share the workload, and each person will be accountable for their task.
turns.translation: Kedengarannya adil. Kita bisa membagi beban kerja, dan setiap orang akan bertanggung jawab atas tugasnya.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a time you shared responsibilities with other people.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Tell me about a time you worked with other people and shared the tasks.
storyPoints: Describe the project or activity and the people involved.
Explain how you divided the work and who was accountable for each task.
Say what went well or what you would change next time.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: We shared the workload fairly, and each person was accountable for one part of the project.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wiː ʃeəd ðə ˈwɜːkləʊd ˈfeəli, ən iːtʃ ˈpɜːsən wəz əˈkaʊntəbl fə wʌn pɑːt əv ðə ˈprɒdʒekt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Tell the story in a clear order. Use the past simple for completed actions and include details about who did each task.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Speak for at least 30 seconds about a job or team role you know.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe a job you know and explain the main responsibilities of the person in that role.
storyPoints: Name the job and describe its main duties.
Explain who the person works with and what they oversee.
Say which skills or habits help the person do the job well.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: A team leader oversees daily work, delegates tasks, and checks that deadlines are met.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ə tiːm ˈliːdə ˌəʊvəˈsiːz ˈdeɪli wɜːk, ˈdelɪɡeɪts tɑːsks, ən tʃeks ðət ˈdedlaɪnz ə met/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Describe the role with full sentences. Use present simple verbs to explain regular responsibilities.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Take part in a short call. Suggest who should prepare the report and explain how you will check it.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: We need to finish the client report this week. Who can prepare it, and who will check the final version?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: Your team is planning a client report during a video call. The report is due on Friday, and the manager wants clear task ownership.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a project coordinator. Suggest a colleague to prepare the first draft and say who will review it.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I will get Maya to prepare the first draft, and I can check it on Thursday.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wɪl ɡet ˈmaɪə tə prɪˈpeə ðə fɜːst drɑːft, ən aɪ kən tʃek ɪt ɒn ˈθɜːzdeɪ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use get plus a person plus to and a base verb. Give a practical deadline and identify who will check the work.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to the team member and delegate one suitable task using have.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: I have finished the schedule. What would you like me to do next?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: A colleague has completed the team schedule. You need them to review the job descriptions before the afternoon meeting.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the team manager. Ask your colleague to review the job descriptions and tell them when you need the work.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I will have you review the job descriptions before two o'clock.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wɪl hæv juː rɪˈvjuː ðə dʒɒb dɪˈskrɪpʃənz bɪˈfɔː tuː əˈklɒk/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use have plus a person plus the base verb. Make the task and its deadline clear and polite.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Explain how you will share the work and make sure each person has a clear responsibility.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Two people have too much work, while another team member has time. How can we share the tasks?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are in a team meeting. The workload is uneven, and the group needs to agree on a fair plan.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are a team member. Suggest one way to redistribute tasks and name who will oversee the progress.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Let's ask Jordan to take the data check, and I can oversee the progress.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /lets ɑːsk ˈdʒɔːdən tə teɪk ðə ˈdeɪtə tʃek, ən aɪ kən ˌəʊvəˈsiː ðə ˈprəʊɡres/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Offer a fair plan and say who will be responsible for each part. Use a clear and cooperative tone.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Respond to the manager. Explain what the deadline requires and how you will organise the work.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: The client needs the updated report tomorrow. Can you make sure the team finishes it on time?
practicumQuestions.scenarioContext: You are speaking with your manager by phone. A client has moved the deadline forward, so the team must organise its tasks quickly.
practicumQuestions.characterRole: You are the project assistant. Explain how the team can prioritise the report and ask a colleague to help.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I will make the team prioritise the client report, and I will get Alex to check the figures.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ wɪl meɪk ðə tiːm praɪˈɒrətaɪz ðə ˈklaɪənt rɪˈpɔːt, ən aɪ wɪl ɡet ˈæleks tə tʃek ðə ˈfɪɡəz/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use make plus a person or group plus the base verb. Use get plus a person plus to and a verb for the second task.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Use delegate, job description, oversee, accountable, workload, and prioritise in short workplace sentences.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Describe how a manager can divide work and help a team meet its deadlines.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: A manager can delegate tasks, oversee the work, and help everyone prioritise their workload.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /ə ˈmænɪdʒə kən ˈdelɪɡeɪt tɑːsks, ˌəʊvəˈsiː ðə wɜːk, ən help ˈevriwʌn praɪˈɒrətaɪz ðeə ˈwɜːkləʊd/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use each word in a sentence that shows its workplace meaning. Speak clearly and connect the vocabulary to responsibilities.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one sentence with have, one with make, and one with get to describe arranging work.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: How would you ask or arrange for other people to complete three different team tasks?
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: I had Rosa check the figures, made the team finish the plan, and got Amir to call the client.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /aɪ hæd ˈrəʊzə tʃek ðə ˈfɪɡəz, meɪd ðə tiːm ˈfɪnɪʃ ðə plæn, ən ɡɒt əˈmɪə tə kɔːl ðə ˈklaɪənt/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Use have or make plus a person plus the base verb. Use get plus a person plus to and the base verb.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Repeat the words delegate, accountable, oversee, and prioritise. Make the stressed syllable clear in each word.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Listen to the words, then say them with the main stress in the right place.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: We delegate fairly, stay accountable, oversee the work, and prioritise urgent tasks.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /wiː ˈdelɪɡeɪt ˈfeəli, steɪ əˈkaʊntəbl, ˌəʊvəˈsiː ðə wɜːk, ən praɪˈɒrətaɪz ˈɜːdʒənt tɑːsks/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Stress the first syllable in delegate, the second in accountable, the final syllable in oversee, and the second syllable in prioritise.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Say one yes-or-no question with rising intonation, then give an instruction or statement with falling intonation.
practicumQuestions.audioPrompt: Ask a colleague to take a task, then confirm the deadline.
practicumQuestions.targetSentence: Can you check the report? Please send it by Thursday.
practicumQuestions.phonetic: /kən juː tʃek ðə rɪˈpɔːt? pliːz send ɪt baɪ ˈθɜːzdeɪ/
practicumQuestions.explanation: Let your voice rise slightly at the end of the yes-or-no question. Let it fall at the end of the clear instruction.
